description:

courses to Northeastern University and neighboring communities; and it participates
as an active member in partnerships of local community groups and government
agencies.

A pre-requisite training with the goal of raising awareness of the importance of security and security controls. Situational awareness training is the improvement of someone's perception of environmental elements and events, the comprehension of their meaning, and the projection of their future status.

This training is also available in Spanish

title: Arlington Chamber of Commerce: Young Professionals Happy Hour
description:
This series for the supports young professionals that work or live in Arlington. The program engages the next generation of leaders and provides them with opportunities to develop the skills to be successful leaders in the community. Connecting young professionals with the broader business community aims to deepen their ties, helping our community with workforce development and retention.

Transporation

Parking is available at the parking garage under the Alamo, with entrances on 18th Street and Crystal Drive.

The venue is also located two blocks from the Crystal City Metro Station on the Blue/Yellow Line.

Registration

$20 to register. Registration closes at noon on Wednesday, August 12. For registration questions, please contact DJ Batchelor, Operations Manager, at chamber@arlingtonchamber.org or 703-525-2400. 

Prospective members are allowed to attend up to three (3) Chamber Networking (Breakfast Connection, Business After Business, Small Business Roundtable, Women in Business Networking) events as a guest.

Registrations are non-refundable. While you are unable to apply registrations to future events, you may transfer your registration to another individual.

title: Women's Foreign Policy Group - Bridging the Gap: Successful Coalition-Building in Youth, Peace, and Security
description:
Please join the Women's Foreign Policy Group virtually on Thursday, August 13th from 12:00 PM - 1:00 PM ET for "Bridging the Gap: Successful Coalition-Building in Youth, Peace, and Security," a virtual discussion that seeks to examine how stakeholders can move beyond policy commitments toward meaningful action that strengthens youth leadership in peacebuilding and security, directly hearing from prominent experts in peacebuilding, youth engagement, and global security.

Our esteemed panelists include:


  • Caitlin Dallaire, Senior Nonresident Fellow, New Lines Institute for Strategy and Policy; Founder/Host, The Public Service Project podcast; former Peacekeeping Advisor; U.S. Department of State
  • Sarah Sladen, Senior Fellow, Georgetown University Collaborative on Global Children’s Issues; former Youth Coordinator, USAID

title: WIT - From Burnout to Breakthrough: The Mindset Reset for Women in Tech
description:
Many high-achieving women believe that success comes from learning more, working harder, and collecting more credentials. But research and real-world experience show something surprising: up to 80% of success is driven by mindset — how you think, respond to challenges, and show up every day.

In fast-moving industries like technology, constant pressure, high expectations, and nonstop change can quietly lead to stress, exhaustion, and burnout, even for the most passionate professionals.

In this engaging and empowering session, Edyta Satchell, wellness expert and entrepreneur, shares how women can recognize early signs of burnout, protect their well-being, and rebuild the mindset needed to thrive in demanding careers.

Participants will discover how to:


  • Recognize the hidden signs of burnout before they take over
  • Rebuild energy, focus, and emotional resilience in high-pressure environments
  • Strengthen confidence and overcome self-doubt or imposter syndrome
  • Develop a healthier relationship with money, success, and opportunity
  • Reconnect with purpose and fall in love with their career again


This session blends mindset strategy, wellness insights, and practical tools to help women create sustainable success without sacrificing their health or happiness.

Attendees will leave feeling re-energized, empowered, and ready to step into the next level of their career with clarity and confidence.

Registration Fees
FREE for WIT Members
$25 for Non-members

title: DevFestDC 2026: Build Edition
description:
Join 800+ developers at the highly anticipated DevFest DC returns on August 28, 2026, at GMU Fuse at Mason Square!






Join 800+ Developers at DevFest DC 2026!


 


The DMV's Largest Developer Conference Returns for Year 14!


Google Developers Group Washington D.C. 14th annual DevFest DC - the largest #DevTech event in North America carefully crafted by and for the DC, Maryland and Virginia developer community!


 


WHAT MAKES DEVFEST DC SPECIAL?


  • 800+ passionate developers from across the DMV
  • World-class speakers from Google & top tech companies
  • Hands-on learning through sessions, code labs, and interactive workshops
  • Multiple tracks tailored to your interests and career goals
  • Unmatched networking opportunities with industry leaders and peers

 


FEATURED SPEAKERS:


Our curated lineup includes industry and local community experts who are shaping the future of technology:


  • Building in the AI-first world: Scale brilliance, not bottlenecks - Nathen Harvey , DORA Lead at Google
  • Two Tablets, One Bench: Real-Time Multiplayer at the Edge with Durable Objects and Workers AI - Amanda J Kendal-Brown, Capital One
  • AppFunctions: Making Your Android App Agent-Ready - Chrystian Vieyra Cortes, Thomson Reuters
  • #AirClaw: Build Self-Healing Agents with Apache Airflow and NVIDIA NemoClaw - Chanel Power, Mentor Me Collective
  • From Bookshelf to Borderline: Building a Multi-Agent AI That Turns Books Into Travel - Olga Ostrovskiy, My Storyland
  • Systems That Settle: Control Theory for Adaptive AI - Santosh Srinivasaiah, Diaconia
  • Kubernetes Node Autoscaling w/ Karpenter - Brandon Wagner, Oxide Computer Company
  • Lessons from Shipping a Real App: Vibe Coding in Production - Meheret Egzerab, Studio Rehoboth
  • Build the same AI agent in six frameworks and learn which one actually fits your problem - Kiruthika Subramani, Bell Lab (Code Labs)
  • Build AI agents your compliance team will actually approve - Kiruthika Subramani, Bell Lab (Code Labs)
  • Great Maps Don't Happen by Accident: Building Exceptional Location Experiences with the Mapbox Android SDKs - Chris Whong, Mapbox

 


CONTENT TRACKS:


We will have 20+ sessions and code-labs with great content happening across the day around these three core tracks of content. Get ready for inspiring keynotes, impactful hands-on workshops, and world class speakers!


  • AI & Data
  • Agents & Robotics
  • Programming Languages & Framework
  • Startup Innovation

 


LOCATION & GETTING THERE:


FUSE Center at George Mason University

Address: 3351 Fairfax Dr, Arlington, VA 22201 (Map)

We strongly recommend using public transportation or a ride-sharing service for your convenience

Metro: Take the Orange/Silver Line to Virginia Square-GMU station (2-minute walk)

For on-site limited parking, you can find paid options at Van Metre Hall Parking Garage and Vernon Smith Parking Garage. There are also a few street parking spots available.

 


READY TO ATTEND?


With 800+ developers expected, tickets go fast.

Register now to guarantee your place at the DMV's most anticipated developer event.

Stay Connected:


  • Latest updates: devfestdc.org
  • Follow us LinkedIn @Instagram @X/Twitter @Facebook
  • # Hashtag #DevFestDC

Questions? Email us at info@devfestdc.org

title: Rosslyn Jazz Fest 2026
description:
Arlington, Virginia’s most popular free outdoor music festival is back on Saturday, Sept. 12!






Join the Rosslyn BID and Arlington Arts at the 34th Rosslyn Jazz Fest 2026 in Arlington, VA for free live jazz, funk & soul, food trucks, local vendors, and family-friendly outdoor entertainment near Washington, D.C. One of the largest cultural events in Arlington, Jazz Fest is the best way to end the summer!


Getting There


 


Parking


Parking at Rosslyn Jazz Fest is limited — we encourage you to take public transportation.

If you do plan to drive, several parking garages in the neighborhood offer weekend parking. For street parking, refer to Arlington County's Interactive Parking Meter Map.


Public Transportation


The Rosslyn Metro Station is less than a 5-minute walk to Gateway Park, and is served by the Orange, Silver, and Blue Metro lines. There are also numerous buses, including the Arlington ART and Metrobus, that make stops close to the park!


Rideshare


We recommend marking your drop-off location as Roll Play (1800 N. Lynn St.) — it's just one block south of Gateway Park and avoids day-of festival road closures.


Biking


For a person-powered option to get to Jazz Fest, grab a bike from Capital Bikeshare and dock at one of our many area bike racks.

Please note: A photographer may be on-site at this event. By attending, you consent for your image to be used for future Rosslyn BID marketing or promotional purposes.

title: WIT.Connect Evening Event: Lessons in Leadership: Insights from the Front Lines
description:
Join us for a dynamic and engaging panel discussion that brings together accomplished leaders ready to share their most valuable lessons learned along the way. Whether you’re just starting your leadership journey or looking to grow in your current role, this event will provide you with authentic stories, practical strategies, and inspiration you can immediately put into practice.

Our panelists will explore the challenges and triumphs that have shaped their careers, from the advice they would give their younger selves to the leadership obstacles they’ve overcome. Expect candid conversations about resilience, navigating setbacks, and celebrating meaningful achievements—all with the goal of helping you embrace your own path with confidence.

Don’t miss this opportunity to connect with peers, gain perspective, and walk away with actionable insights on mentorship, leadership growth, and building strong support networks. Reserve your seat today and be part of a conversation designed to inspire and empower the leaders of tomorrow.

$25 WIT Member
$35 Non-members
